wPCA Explorer

One known deposit is enough. Give it one area you know holds a deposit; it learns that deposit's geometry in the geophysical maps and ranks every other area by how closely it matches. Like reverse image search for a map. Open, validated, and running entirely in your browser. Method: Mantilla Salas et al. (2026), Natural Resources Research.
Sofia Mantilla Salas
Stanford Mineral-X
Code DOI
Reproducible by construction. At Paper 200 m (exact) the default run reproduces Case 1 to the digit: 47.0% recovery · AUC 57.9 · 5 of 11 deposits. The 400 m preview answers in seconds.
Your data never leaves your computer. A single static page — no backend, no uploads, no analytics; zero network requests after load (verify in the Network tab). Save the file and it runs fully offline.

New here? Give it one area you know holds a deposit; it finds the look alikes and rediscovers ones hidden from it.

1 Window

A deposit-sized window slides across the grid. Every position becomes one observation.

2 Learn

PCA distils each window to a few components; those most characteristic of the reference deposit carry the weight.

3 Rank

Every window is scored by how closely it reproduces the reference deposit's geophysical geometry — closest first.

4 Validate

The ranking is tested against independent test-deposit footprints, versus a random selection of equal area.

Footprint recoveredFor each test deposit, the share of its footprint covered by the selected windows — averaged over the deposits.
–
Test deposits hitA test deposit counts as hit once the selected windows cover at least 50% of its footprint.
–
Recovery AUCArea under the cumulative recovery curve. It rewards recovering footprint early in the ranking, not only by the final window.
–
Area selectedTotal ground area of the selected windows, with overlaps merged so shared ground is counted once.
–
vs random of matched areaFootprint recovered divided by the share of the study area selected. 1× is chance; 2× means twice what a random selection of the same area would recover.
–

Cumulative footprint recoveryHow much test-deposit footprint is recovered as you accept more windows in rank order. The dashed line and grey band show a random selection of equal area (mean, 5–95%).

Top 10 prediction windowsThe ten highest-ranked windows by weighted PCA distance to the reference deposit. Distance is unitless — smaller means a closer match.

Bring your own grids

The same six steps, on your data. Every file is parsed and analysed by your own browser — nothing is transmitted, stored, or logged anywhere. Confidential exploration data stays exactly where it is.

1 · Grids (required)
GeoTIFF, one file per variable, up to 5 — e.g. TMI.tif, U.tif, gravity.tif. Same size, cell and origin; projected CRS in metres. Stripped (untiled), uncompressed or DEFLATE. Multi-band files are supported — pick which band a variable uses, and reuse the same file in several rows to combine its bands. (Geosoft grid and XYZ/CSV planned.)
2 · Deposit outlines (optional)
deposits.geojson — polygons with a name property, same CRS as the grids. (Zipped shapefile planned.) No outline files? Add deposits on the map instead: click a point + size, or drag to draw — for the reference window and the test deposits alike.

Verifiably private. After the page loads, the app makes zero network requests — open your browser's Network tab and watch, or save the page and run it with the internet disconnected. The hosting server only ever delivers the page; it never sees your data.
Mantilla Salas, S., Mejia-Herrera, P., Kloeckner, J., Asadi, A., Yin, D. Z., & Caers, J. (2026). Geometry-based targeting from a single known deposit using windowed principal component analysis: an IOCG case study in Carajás, Brazil. Natural Resources Research.
